claim: Reviews work offline after the first visit
sandbox: fresh Chromium context at /demo; wait for the service worker, reload once, then set the context offline and reload

claim: Demo never reads or writes real notes or license storage, and every exit discards sample changes
sandbox: fresh browser context; seed a real library and license, use /?demo=1&license=..., byte-compare real storage, then change a sample before the visible Restore, checkout, and Start for real exits and confirm each restores five clips and three due questions

claim: The demo starts with five sample clips and Reset demo restores them
sandbox: fresh /demo context; assert five authored clips and three due questions, change one, reset, then assert the original counts return

claim: An RSS feed can fill the podcast and episode fields
sandbox: fresh browser context at /demo with a locally fulfilled RSS response

claim: The app contacts a feed address only after Find episodes is pressed
sandbox: fresh browser context at /demo; fill a private fixture feed address, assert zero requests before activation, then press Find episodes and assert exactly one request to that address

claim: An Atom feed can fill the podcast, episode, and link fields
sandbox: fresh browser context at /demo with a locally fulfilled Atom response; assert the exact podcast, episode, and link values

claim: The daily recall queue presents no more than three due questions
where: landing, app heading, README, catalog description
sandbox: fresh /demo sample with all five clips made overdue before the daily snapshot; complete three, reload into the caught-up state, then advance the stored local day and assert the two deferred clips appear

claim: Exports saved clips as CSV
sandbox: fresh /demo sample; assert the downloaded CSV header and five data rows

claim: Exports saved clips as Markdown
sandbox: fresh /demo sample; assert all five prompt headings in the downloaded Markdown

claim: The free library accepts eight clips
sandbox: fresh /demo sample; add three clips, then assert a ninth clip is refused

claim: Reviews and exports stay free
sandbox: fresh /demo context with no license; complete a review and download a CSV export

claim: Saved note flows send no note data or tracking requests to another origin
where: landing privacy facts, privacy page, README
sandbox: fresh /app library; observe every request while saving, reloading, exporting, importing, and deleting a real note, then assert all are same-origin

claim: The demo recall flow works without an account
sandbox: fresh /demo context with no stored credentials; complete a review and assert there are no sign-in controls or authentication requests

claim: Saved questions stay in this browser after a reload
sandbox: fresh /app library; save a question, reload the page, and assert the exact question remains

claim: The app stores written podcast metadata and notes, not audio
sandbox: fresh /demo sample; assert there are no audio or video elements, no media requests, and no audio or transcript fields in stored clips

claim: Listeners write their own recall questions and takeaways
sandbox: fresh /app library; enter exact question and takeaway text, save, reveal, and assert both strings are unchanged

claim: A JSON backup exports and restores the complete clip library
sandbox: fresh /demo sample; export five clips, delete one, import the downloaded bytes, and assert all five return

claim: An invalid backup file leaves saved clips unchanged
sandbox: fresh /app library; save one question, import the parseable wrong-shaped file {"clips":[{}]}, reload, then assert the question remains and no page error occurred

claim: A recalled question leaves today's queue and remains scheduled after reload
sandbox: fresh /demo sample; mark one of three due questions remembered, assert two remain, reload, and assert two still remain

claim: The next review is based on the answer
sandbox: fresh /demo sample; use Review sooner and I remembered, then assert each removes one question from today’s queue

claim: Downloads a daily calendar reminder for the recall queue
sandbox: fresh /app context; download the calendar file and assert it has a daily rule and a link to /app

claim: The app is installable as a standalone PWA
sandbox: production preview; assert a standalone manifest is available and the service worker controls /demo after activation

claim: An existing valid license removes the eight-clip limit and is checked at most once each day
where: landing price, app limit, privacy and terms pages
sandbox: fresh /app context with a returned fixture license; mock a valid Sociobot response, save nine clips, reload, and assert only one verification request

claim: Unlimited clips cost $9 once through Sociobot checkout
sandbox: fresh browser context at /; intercept the recorded Sociobot checkout fixture, activate purchase, and assert product slug, USD, one-time billing, and 900-cent amount

claim: A buyer can paste a valid license to restore unlimited clips on another device
sandbox: fresh browser context at /; submit a fixture license, mock the Sociobot verification response, and assert the token is stored with an announced success message

claim: The app stores only the license token and its daily verification result for licensing
sandbox: fresh browser context at /; restore a fixture license, then assert the only sb_license:podcast-recall-loop values are the exact token and a {valid, checkedAt} verdict

claim: Installed copies receive every new app build without a manual cache-version edit
sandbox: render the production worker from two HTML shells whose only difference is the fingerprinted app asset; assert distinct worker bytes, cache names, and precache entries

claim: Sociobot handles checkout for the one-time license
sandbox: fresh browser context at /; assert the purchase uses the Sociobot product endpoint and no payment-provider link is embedded
